prose_updates.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, the paper identifies the reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient as an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects and gives support-only rank and exact forward diagnostics. On the full-rank probability-floor domain, the complete loading image is a compact semialgebraic body. A terminating exact real-algebraic procedure decides target membership and returns either an algebraic feasible law or an attained closest loading, a metric-separation certificate, and exact worst-case contamination over coordinatewise bounded effects; generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition is potentially doubly exponential. The separate published unit-indexed layer retains the tensor approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), with a block witness showing that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from its stated conditions. The remaining open problem is a support-uniform ordered/combinatorial description of chamber counts, signs, incidences, and simultaneous off-diagonal-zero strata, not finite-instance decidability.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory establishes dynamic consistency under calendar-homogeneous effects and leaves its calendar-varying DATE equation beyond scope. Its class and the base i.i.d. conditional-mean layer remain incomparable. Existing event-study decompositions and supplied-law numerical diagnostics do not provide the complete finite-memory calendar-by-lag loading body, exact inverse membership, certified closest loading, or exact bounded-effect contamination on an arbitrary listed support.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are an arbitrary-path loading tensor shared algebraically across two explicitly separated sampling layers and an exact finite-instance inverse analysis that respects probability-product compatibility on every exceptional stratum. Ordered absorption structure remains useful for a sharper structural chamber law, but is not needed for exact decidability.
project_justification.fill: The project proves arbitrary-path covariance and pair-mass identities, exact normalization, rational supplied-law diagnostics, and the positive-law support-rank law. It encodes the complete full-rank probability-floor loading body by its polynomial probability-vector graph, proves compact semialgebraicity and uniform invertibility, and uses exact real-algebraic elimination to return membership witnesses or an attained closest loading with a metric-separation certificate and exact bounded-effect worst-case contamination. The generic algorithm terminates but may be doubly exponential and does not replace the open ordered/combinatorial chamber classification. In the separate published triangular-array layer, the calendar-varying tensor approximation remains \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and the block construction rules out any uniformly faster rate from the stated conditions alone.

sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite binary-path support \(\mathcal S\), rational probability floor \(\epsilon\), and positive ex ante reshaping law. The inverse analysis ranges over the entire compact floor domain and uses the probability-vector polynomial graph, so all pair-product compatibility constraints are retained. Absorption is required only for the ordered Green, graph-rank, and adjacent-ratio corollaries. In the separate published layer, taking \(\mathcal S=\mathcal S^*\) reproduces the published support exactly.

prose_updates.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known generalized propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence. The base i.i.d. conditional-mean class is not their published class and is incomparable with it. The separate unit-indexed theorem retains their class exactly upon taking the reshaping support to be \(\mathcal S^*\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying finite-memory effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and directly recovers their homogeneous theorem; its block construction shows that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from their stated conditions alone. Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients but do not analyze assignment-law reshaping or its complete inverse image. Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) motivate treatment-history indexing under known experimental assignment, while de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) study time-constant random-coefficient distributed lags. Wright (2026) supplies adjacent numerical diagnostic evidence and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) supply time-varying distributed-lag modeling precedent; none supplies the present exact probability-graph loading body, membership or metric-separation certificate, and closest-loading bounded-effect contamination calculation. Collins (1975) supplies the standard generic cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition algorithm; the contribution here is the exact loading-tensor encoding and certified inverse analysis, not generic quantifier elimination itself.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The forward tensor algebra and exact loading-body inverse procedure cover arbitrary finite binary-path supports. In the nonsingular support branch the probability floor yields uniform invertibility, compactness, attainment, and exact real-algebraic membership or metric-separation certificates; feasible and optimizing laws may be algebraic rather than rational. The closest loading uses the declared tensor \(\ell_1\) diagnostic, and bounded-effect contamination is minimized secondarily only among its minimizers. Generic cylindrical algebraic decomposition is exact and terminating but potentially doubly exponential; no convexity, linear separating hyperplane, polynomial-time method, or closed support-uniform structural chamber law is claimed. The ordered/combinatorial enumeration of chamber counts, loading signs, boundary incidences, and simultaneous off-diagonal-zero strata remains open. The separate published triangular-array theorem proves the coefficient approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\) and shows that no uniformly faster rate follows from the stated conditions. No central limit theorem, asymptotic normality, cross-fitted robust inference, or empirical application is supplied.
